title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How Electric Car Salary Sacrifice Affects Your Take-Home Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our guide. Includes electric car salary sacrifice, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, or any deductions. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, so a casual employee receives $33.05 per hour including the loading. When converting to annual pay, use the casual rate (including loading) in the formula.

faqs.q: How does an electric car salary sacrifice arrangement affect my tax and super?
faqs.a: An electric car salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering the tax you pay. However, super guarantee contributions are generally calculated on your ordinary earnings, which may be reduced after salary sacrifice. The Australian Taxation Office sets rules for salary sacrifice, and your employer must still pay super on your ordinary time earnings. Always check the impact on your total remuneration package.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Pay

Knowing how your hourly wage translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. This guide explains the conversion formula, the role of casual loading, superannuation, and tax, and how an electric car salary sacrifice arrangement can change your take-home pay.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The standard method to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard under the Fair Work Act), the formula becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparison, not a binding determination of your pay.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you align your budget with your pay cycle.

### Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Casual Loading

Australia has several pay benchmarks:

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific minimum rates set by the Fair Work Commission. These are often higher than the national minimum.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of the base rate. For the national minimum, a casual earns $33.05 per hour. When converting to annual pay, use the casual rate (including loading) in the formula.
- **Superannuation**: Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your employer contributes an additional $3.60 per hour to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

### How Electric Car Salary Sacrifice Fits In

An electric car salary sacrifice arrangement allows you to pay for a car (and running costs) from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. This can lower the tax you pay, but it also reduces your ordinary earnings for super guarantee purposes. The Australian Taxation Office sets rules for salary sacrifice; your employer must still pay super on your ordinary time earnings, which may be lower after the sacrifice.

For example, if your base hourly rate is $40 and you salary sacrifice $200 per week for an electric car, your taxable income drops, but your super contributions (12% of ordinary earnings) may also drop if your ordinary earnings are reduced. Always model the net effect using [the timesheet](/) or consult a tax professional.

### Tax and Medicare

The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This is an estimate only.

### Superannuation Guarantee

From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost for your employer. When comparing job offers, consider the total package including super.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Calculations

To see how your hourly rate converts to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, use [the timesheet](/). You can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add 25% casual loading. The timesheet assumes a 38-hour week unless you adjust it. Remember: never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; let the tool add it.

### Further Resources

For award-specific rates, visit [pay guides](/blog). For detailed tax tables and super rules, see [reference tables](/data). The Fair Work Ombudsman provides official pay and conditions information. The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings: full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, while all employees (including part-time) earned $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job.

Always check your employment contract and seek professional advice for your individual circumstances.
